paper.title: An efficient algorithm for contextual bandits with knapsacks, and an extension to concave objectives

settings.name_in_paper: CBwK (Contextual Bandits with Knapsacks) / Resourceful Contextual Bandits
unmapped: d-dimensional resource consumption vectors in [0,1]^d observed for chosen action; algorithm stops when any budget is exceeded
no-op action and no-op policy assumed
finite policy class Pi accessed through an arg-max oracle (AMO); comparator is best mixed policy over Pi feasible in expectation
settings.definition_quote: in every round $t\in [T]$, the algorithm observes context $x_t \in X$, chooses an action $a_t \in A$, and observes a reward $r_t(a_t)\in[0,1]$ and a $\di$-dimensional consumption vector $\cv_t(a_t) \in [0,1]^\di$. The objective is to take actions that maximize the total reward ... while making sure that ... $\sum_{t=1}^T \cv_t(a_t) \leq B\ones$. ... $(x_t, \{r_t (a), \cv_t(a):a \in A\})$ ... are drawn i.i.d. from a distribution ${\cal D}$

unmapped: vector-valued outcomes in [0,1]^d; objective is a known L-Lipschitz concave function f of the average outcome vector
the learner knows the function f (given ahead of time)
finite policy class Pi accessed through an arg-max oracle; comparator is best mixed policy over Pi
settings.definition_quote: The outcome in a round is simply the vector $\cv$, and the goal of the algorithm is to maximize $f(\frac 1 T \sum_{t=1} \cv_t(a_t))$, for some concave function $f$ defined on the domain $[0,1]^\di$, and given to the algorithm ahead of time.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1 adapted for CBwR (no initial exploration, concave-objective empirical regret)

symbols.OPT: value T*R(P*) of the best static mixed policy feasible in expectation

conditions: B > c' sqrt(K T ln(dT|Pi|/delta)) for a large enough constant c'
no-op action and no-op policy exist
finite policy class Pi with arg max oracle access

source.label: thm:packing
source.quote: For the \Cbudget~ problem, $\forall \delta >0$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that makes $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{KT\ln(|\Pi|)})$ calls to AMO, and with probability at least $1-\delta$ has regret $$ \regret(T) = O\left( \frac{\OPT}{B}  +1 \right)\sqrt{{K T \ln(dT|\Pi|/\delta)} }.$$

results.notes: Regret is OPT minus realized total reward. Polynomial time given an AMO, using O~(d sqrt(KT ln|Pi|)) oracle calls. Improves Badanidiyuru et al. (2014) by sqrt(d).

symbols.norm_1d: norm ||1_d|| of the all-ones vector in the norm w.r.t. which f is Lipschitz

conditions: f is concave and L-Lipschitz w.r.t. norm ||.||
problems max f(x)+a.x over [0,1]^d solvable in polynomial time
finite policy class Pi with arg max oracle access

source.label: th:General
source.quote: For the \CBwR~ problem, if $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz w.r.t. norm $\|\cdot\|$, then there is a polynomial time algorithm that makes $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{KT\ln(|\Pi|)})$ calls to AMO, and with probability at least $1-\delta$ has regret $$\areg(T) = O\left( \frac{\oneNorm L}{\sqrt{T}} \left(\sqrt{K \ln(T|\Pi|/\delta)} + \sqrt{\ln(d/\delta)} \right) \right).$$

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret OPT - f(average outcome); expression multiplied by T per extraction rules. Proof notes the simpler form assumes T >= K ln(T|Pi|/delta) (otherwise trivial).
